facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's policy states that birth and death registration is run by its Bureau of Vital Statistics under a Principal Registrar reporting to the Assistant Minister for Vital Statistics, with county and district registrars beneath, under the Public Health Law of 1976.
facts.system: Birth and death registration system (Bureau of Vital Statistics)

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health states that the Bureau of Vital Statistics has 24 staff whose basic salaries are funded by the national budget under the ministry, that donors and partners also contribute significantly, and that the national allocation has been inadequate.
facts.system: Birth and death registration system (Bureau of Vital Statistics)

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health issued this Birth and Death Registration and Certification Policy in November 2017, with UNICEF technical and financial support, and cites a CRVS investment case for 2016-2020 and CRVS and birth registration improvement plans holding its monitoring framework; none of them is described as naming a digital system.
facts.system: Birth and death registration system (Bureau of Vital Statistics)

systems.system: Birth and death registration system (Bureau of Vital Statistics)
systems.country_label: Register of Births; Register of Death; BR and DR databases
systems.owner: Ministry of Health, Bureau of Vital Statistics (Principal Registrar)
systems.tiers: Principal Registrar nationally; county and district registrars; registration centres at clinics, health centres, hospitals, district and county health offices and county service centres; decentralised to all counties except Montserrado
Defined only: registration by SMS, mobile phone app or web application, or by moving teams; no deployment described
Health facility record of a newborn's birth; community health workers to track and notify community births and deaths

note: The policy does not say how the record is made: a Registration Assistant records the form in the Register of Births or of Death, a lost certificate is replaced by searching the registry and printing, and 'BR and DR databases' are named as monitoring tools, with no statement of where data entry happens. No events, made or offices fact taken. Coverage figures (births registered 2007-2016, 6.5% of facility deaths registered in 2012) are shares of events, not offices.
